title: Single- And Two-mode Magnon Thermal Squeezing
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: Thermal squeezing of magnons is demonstrated in a ferrimagnetic insulator device, achieving noise below thermal levels.
motivation: To realize squeezed states in magnets for spin-based sensing and information technology.
method: Experimental demonstration in a ferrimagnetic insulator device, likely using microwave techniques to generate and detect magnon squeezing.
result: Observation of single- and two-mode magnon thermal squeezing, with noise dropping below thermal levels.
conclusion: This work opens avenues for quantum-enhanced sensing and information processing using magnons in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Suppression Of Coherent Light Scattering In A Three-dimensional Atomic Array
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: Experiments with a three-dimensional atomic array demonstrate strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering.
motivation: Most studies of collective light scattering in atomic arrays have focused on one- and two-dimensional systems; extending to three dimensions is important for fundamental understanding and potential applications.
method: Experimental realization of a three-dimensional atomic array and measurement of coherent light scattering properties.
result: Strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering was observed in the 3D array.
conclusion: This work opens new possibilities for controlling light-matter interactions in three-dimensional atomic arrays, with implications for quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hong–Ou–Mandel Interference Of More Than Ten Indistinguishable Atoms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstration of Hong–Ou–Mandel interference with up to 12 indistinguishable neutral atoms, showing multiparticle interference patterns with single-atom resolution.
motivation: Extending HOM interference to many massive particles is challenging; this work aims to observe multiparticle interference in a controlled atomic ensemble.
method: Experiments with up to 12 neutral atoms in an optical trap, using single-atom detection to measure interference patterns.
result: Characteristic multiparticle interference patterns observed with negligible loss, demonstrating indistinguishability and coherence across many atoms.
conclusion: Enables studies of multiparticle quantum interference and may impact quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and cell density control phase transitions in tissue organization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how mechanical properties like adhesion and jamming regulate tissue material state and developmental programs.
method: Combined in silico modeling and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization.
conclusion: Phase transitions direct developmental programs, highlighting the role of adhesion in tissue organization.

title: Adhesion-driven Rigidity Transition Decoupled From Density-driven Jamming Triggers Epithelial Organization In Embryonic Tissues
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies adhesion-driven rigidity transitions in embryonic tissues, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how mechanical properties like rigidity influence tissue organization during morphogenesis.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of cell adhesion and density in embryonic tissues.
result: Adhesion-driven rigidification is key to epithelial organization and is decoupled from density-driven jamming.
conclusion: Provides insights into tissue mechanics but has no direct connection to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.

title: Thorium-229 Lifetime Locked Down
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper resolves a decade-long discrepancy in the lifetime of a nuclear metastable state in thorium-229 ions, revealing an uncommon decay channel.
motivation: The lifetime of the nuclear metastable state in singly charged thorium-229 ions appeared shorter than theoretical predictions, puzzling physicists for about ten years.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis were used to determine the lifetime and identify the decay channel.
result: The solution provides a hint towards an uncommon decay channel, explaining the observed shorter lifetime.
conclusion: The findings resolve the lifetime puzzle and may have implications for nuclear clocks and fundamental physics.

title: Scaling Matters Of Cell Fate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a universal scaling law in DNA methylation dynamics during early embryo development, suggesting physical constraints govern cell fate.
motivation: To understand whether molecular specifics or physical principles determine cell differentiation patterns in early embryos.
method: Analysis of methylation dynamics data from early embryos, fitting to scaling laws.
result: Methylation dynamics follow a universal scaling law, independent of molecular details.
conclusion: Physical constraints, rather than molecular specifics, shape cell fate, with implications for developmental biology.

title: Evidence For The Generic Existence Of Two Local Structures In Liquid Water
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: Simulations suggest the existence of two interconvertible local structures in liquid water, supporting the two-state picture of deeply undercooled water.
motivation: To provide evidence for the long-predicted two-state regime in deeply undercooled water.
result: Two distinct local structures that undergo interconvertible reactions were identified.
conclusion: The findings corroborate the two-state picture of water, with implications for understanding water's anomalous properties.
